author: hugzeal
body:
## Overview
This PR introduces two major features to enhance the marketplace functionality and user trust:

### 🔧 Dispute Resolution System
- **Arbitrator Registration**: Allows trusted users to become dispute arbitrators
- **Dispute Creation**: Buyers can create disputes for problematic transactions
- **Resolution Process**: Arbitrators can fairly resolve disputes and distribute escrowed funds
- **Incentive System**: Arbitrators earn rewards and reputation for resolving disputes

### ⭐ Seller Reputation & Rating System  
- **Seller Profiles**: Comprehensive tracking of seller performance metrics
- **Transaction Ratings**: Buyers can rate sellers (1-5 stars) with written reviews
- **Reputation Tiers**: Automatic tier assignment (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) based on performance
- **Rating History**: Prevents duplicate ratings and tracks buyer rating activity

## Benefits
- **Increased Trust**: Buyers can make informed decisions based on seller reputation
- **Conflict Resolution**: Disputes can be resolved fairly without manual intervention
- **Quality Incentives**: Sellers are motivated to provide good service for better ratings
- **Platform Growth**: Enhanced trust mechanisms encourage more marketplace participation

## Breaking Changes
None - all new features are additive and don't modify existing functionality.

author: alexwaygood
body:
## Summary

A callable instance attribute is not sufficient for a type to satisfy a protocol with a method member: a method member specified by a protocol `P` must exist on the *meta-type* of `T` for `T` to be a subtype of `P`:

```py
from typing import Callable, Protocol
from ty_extensions import static_assert, is_assignable_to

class SupportsFooMethod(Protocol):
    def foo(self): ...

class SupportsFooAttr(Protocol):
    foo: Callable[..., object]

class Foo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.foo: Callable[..., object] = lambda *args, **kwargs: None

static_assert(not is_assignable_to(Foo, SupportsFooMethod))
static_assert(is_assignable_to(Foo, SupportsFooAttr))
```

There are several reasons why we must enforce this rule:
1. Some methods, such as dunder methods, are always looked up on the class directly. If a class with an `__iter__` instance attribute satisfied the `Iterable` protocol, for example, the `Iterable` protocol would not accurately describe the requirements Python has for a class to be iterable at runtime. We _could_ apply different rules for dunder method members as opposed to non-dunder method members, but I worry that this would appear inconsistent and would confuse users.
2. Allowing callable instance attributes to satisfy method members of protocols would make `issubclass()` narrowing of runtime-checkable protocols unsound, as the `issubclass()` mechanism at runtime for protocols only checks whether a method is accessible on the class object, not the instance. (Protocols with non-method members cannot be passed to `issubclass()` at all at runtime.)
3. If we allowed an instance-only attribute to satisfy a method member on a protocol, it would make `type[]` types unsound for protocols. For example, this currently type-checks fine on `main`, but it crashes at runtime; under this PR, it no longer type-checks:

   ```py
   from typing import Protocol
	
   class Foo(Protocol):
       def method(self) -> str: ...
	
	   def f(x: Foo):
	       type(x).method
	
   class Bar:
	   def __init__(self):
	       self.method = lambda: "foo"
	
   f(Bar())
   ```

Enforcing this rule fixes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/764, because the inconsistency between our understanding of `Iterable` assignability and types that `Type::try_iterate()` returned `Ok()` for is now fixed. Many types that we previously incorrectly considered assignable to `Iterable` are now no longer considered assignable to `Iterable`.

## Test plan

- I added mdtests to `protocol.md` explaining and enforcing this rule
- I added a corpus test for https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/764 that ensures that the crash is fixed
- In a PR based on top of this one (https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/19208), I moved `zope.interface` to the `good.txt` list in mypy_primer, and confirmed that this PR means we no longer crash when analyzing that codebase. (Previously, we crashed due to https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/764.)
- I analyzed the mypy_primer report in https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/19187#issuecomment-3052558437. Overall it LGTM.
- The fixes in this PR allow us to stabilise the property test added in https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/19186. I checked that it _is_ stable locally by running `QUICKCHECK_TESTS=1000000 cargo test --release -p ty_python_semantic -- --ignored types::property_tests::stable`
- I also added some failing tests regarding class-literal types where a class has `Any` or `Unknown` in its MRO. I think there's an argument that these _should_ be considered `Iterable` actually, but _not_ because they might have an `__iter__` instance attribute. Rather, the metaclass of such a class might define an `__iter__` method, which would make all classes with that metaclass iterable. We can't come to any firm conclusion about what the metaclass of a class with `Any` in its MRO might be, because the `Any` might materialize to a type with a custom metaclass.

  For now, I defer the question of fixing this, but I have a draft PR open to explore fixing it: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/19157. It has some... surprising primer results. I need to do some more digging there to figure out what's going on. I suspect that there is yet another underlying bug being uncovered there. 😆

## Performance

~~There's a performance regression on this PR, but not a huge one. I think that's sort-of unavoidable; we're again just doing slightly more work than we did before. https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/19230 will more than reclaim the performance hit here, though, if that PR is accepted.~~

After rebasing on #19230, this PR now shows speedups of 3% on some benchmarks, and slowdowns of 2% on others. Overall the picture looks pretty positive to me, but it's hard to make out much signal here: https://codspeed.io/astral-sh/ruff/branches/alex%2Fmethod-metatype?runnerMode=Instrumentation

author: aleenprd
body:
This pull request introduces updates to the CI workflow and Dockerfile to improve build processes, streamline authentication, and enhance the Docker image configuration. Key changes include splitting CI jobs for pull requests and main branch pushes, upgrading GitHub Actions and Docker dependencies, and simplifying the Dockerfile for better maintainability.

### CI Workflow Updates:
* Renamed and split the `docker` job into `docker-pull-request` and `docker-main` to differentiate workflows for pull requests and main branch pushes. Added conditions to ensure appropriate triggers for each job. (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, [.github/workflows/ci.ymlL10-R47](diffhunk://#diff-b803fcb7f17ed9235f1e5cb1fcd2f5d3b2838429d4368ae4c57ce4436577f03fL10-R47))
* Upgraded GitHub Actions dependencies: `google-github-actions/auth` updated to `v2`, and `docker/login-action` updated to `v3`. Adjusted authentication to use `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` instead of `access_token`. (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, [.github/workflows/ci.ymlL32-R82](diffhunk://#diff-b803fcb7f17ed9235f1e5cb1fcd2f5d3b2838429d4368ae4c57ce4436577f03fL32-R82))

### Dockerfile Improvements:
* Switched to the `python:3.12-slim` base image for a smaller and more efficient image. (`Dockerfile`, [DockerfileL1-R31](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R31))
* Simplified user setup by creating a non-root user with a fixed group ID and removing locale configurations. (`Dockerfile`, [DockerfileL1-R31](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R31))
* Updated the installation process for Python dependencies by using `uv` for dependency management instead of `Poetry`. (`Dockerfile`, [DockerfileL1-R31](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R31))
* Streamlined the file structure and copying process, ensuring consistency with the new project directory structure. (`Dockerfile`, [DockerfileL1-R31](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R31))

It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](http://localhost:8080/analysis/fb134fe8-903a-4c19-a0e4-e8f816bae9a5/fix/AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes "OS commands should not be vulnerable to command injection attacks" (id = [pythonsecurity:S2076](https://rules.sonarsource.com/python/RSPEC-2076/)) identified by Sonar. ## Details This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack. Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host. Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application: ```diff import subprocess + from security import safe_command ... - subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True) + safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True) ... - subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"]) + safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"]) ``` The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following: * **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present. * **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration. There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more. ## Dependency Updates This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.
More reading * [https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py) * [https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/OS_Command_Injection_Defense_Cheat_Sheet.html](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/OS_Command_Injection_Defense_Cheat_Sheet.html) * [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20) * [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78) * [OS commands should not be vulnerable to command injection attacks](https://rules.sonarsource.com/python/RSPEC-2076/)

author: dnandakumar-nv
body:
# Description

## 📋 Summary

This PR adds comprehensive support for OpenAI's Responses API to the NeMo Agent toolkit, enabling users to leverage built-in tools (like Code Interpreter) and remote tools via Model Context Protocol (MCP) alongside existing NAT tools.

## ✨ What's New

### Responses API Agent Implementation
- **Native Responses API Clients** - New `api_type` config element for LLMs and supported instantiation of responses API type clients from supported packages. Validation of no-support for others. 
- **New agent type**: `responses_api_agent` that integrates with OpenAI's Responses API
- **Multi-tool support**: Combines NAT tools, OpenAI built-in tools, and MCP remote tools in a single workflow
- **Streaming support**: Full compatibility with Responses API streaming capabilities
- **Error handling**: Configurable tool error handling with graceful fallbacks

### Key Features
- **Built-in tool integration**: Direct support for Code Interpreter, file search, and image generation tools
- **MCP protocol support**: Connect to remote MCP servers with flexible configuration options
- **Tool binding**: Automatic tool binding to LLM with `strict=True` and optional parallel tool calls
- **Validation**: Runtime validation ensuring LLM supports Responses API

## 🔧 Configuration

### Example Configuration
```yaml
llms:
  openai_llm:
    _type: openai
    model_name: gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07
    api_type: responses  # Required for Responses API. Default is `chat_completions`

workflow:
  _type: responses_api_agent
  llm_name: openai_llm
  nat_tools: [current_datetime]
  builtin_tools:
    - type: code_interpreter
      container:
        type: "auto"
  mcp_tools:
    - type: mcp
      server_label: deepwiki
      server_url: https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp
      allowed_tools: [read_wiki_structure, read_wiki_contents]
      require_approval: never
```

### Tool Types Supported
- **`nat_tools`**: NeMo Agent toolkit tools (executed by agent graph)
- **`builtin_tools`**: OpenAI built-in tools (Code Interpreter, file search, image generation)
- **`mcp_tools`**: Remote tools via Model Context Protocol

## 📚 Documentation

### Complete README Section
Added comprehensive documentation covering:
- **What is Responses API**: Clear explanation of capabilities vs Chat Completions
- **Prerequisites**: API key setup and model requirements
- **Usage examples**: CLI commands, server setup, and curl requests
- **Configuration guide**: Detailed explanation of all configuration options
- **Built-in tools**: Code Interpreter setup and other available tools
- **MCP integration**: Complete schema reference and examples
- **Troubleshooting**: Common issues and solutions

### Code Examples
```bash
# Run the agent
nat run --config_file=examples/agents/tool_calling/configs/config-responses-api.yml --input "How many 0s are in the current time?"
```

## 🏗️ Implementation Details

### Files Added/Modified
- **`src/nat/agent/responses_api_agent/register.py`**: Core agent implementation
- **`src/nat/data_models/openai_mcp.py`**: MCP tool schema definitions
- **`examples/agents/tool_calling/configs/config-responses-api.yml`**: Example configuration
- **`examples/agents/tool_calling/README.md`**: Comprehensive documentation
- .... more core library changes and tests

### Technical Architecture
- New support for `api_type` in LLM configurations: One of `chat_completions` or `responses`. 
- New clients for several packages that supports responses API for use in any workflow
- New Agent Leverages existing `ToolCallAgentGraph` for consistent agent behavior
- Binds built-in and MCP tools directly to LLM for Responses API execution
- Maintains separation between NAT tools (graph-executed) and API tools (LLM-executed)
- Supports configurable recursion limits and error handling

## ✅ Testing

### Manual Testing
1. Set OpenAI API key: `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<key>`
2. Run example: `nat run --config_file=examples/agents/tool_calling/configs/config-responses-api.yml --input "How many 0s are in the current time?"`
3. Verify Code Interpreter works: Ask for mathematical calculations or data analysis
4. Test MCP integration: Configure a public MCP server and verify tool calls

### Validation
- ✅ Linting passes (Vale, etc.)
- ✅ Configuration validation works
- ✅ Error handling for unsupported models
- ✅ Documentation formatting correct

## 🚀 Usage

After merging, users can:
1. Configure any supported model with `api_type: responses`
2. Enable Code Interpreter for data analysis and computation
3. Connect to MCP servers for extended functionality
4. Combine multiple tool types in a single workflow
5. Use streaming responses for real-time interaction

## 🔄 Backward Compatibility

- ✅ No breaking changes to existing tool calling agent
- ✅ New agent type is opt-in via configuration
- ✅ Existing examples and workflows unchanged
- ✅ Follows established NAT toolkit patterns

## 📖 Related Documentation

- [OpenAI Responses API Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/responses)
- [Model Context Protocol Specification](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/)

# Java 21 Upgrade Project - Executive Summary  
  
## Executive Summary 📊  
  
Successfully completed comprehensive Java version upgrade from Java 8 to Java 21 for AWS AppConfig Java Sample application. The project utilized automated OpenRewrite tooling combined with Amazon Q CLI assistance to modernize the codebase while maintaining full functionality. All 7 tests pass with zero compilation errors, demonstrating a clean and successful upgrade that preserves business logic while leveraging modern Java capabilities.  
  
## Application Changes 🔄  
  
• **Java Runtime**: Upgraded from Java 8 → Java 21 (LTS)  
• **Spring Boot**: Upgraded from 2.x → 3.0.13 with Jakarta EE migration  
• **Testing Framework**: Migrated from JUnit 4 → JUnit 5 with modern assertions  
• **Mockito**: Updated from 1.x → 4.11.0 with proper generic type handling  
• **Maven Compiler**: Updated to 3.14.0 with Java 21 release configuration  
• **Dependency Management**: Modernized javax → jakarta namespace migration  
  
## Tools Used 🛠️  
  
• **Java SDK**: Amazon Corretto 21.0.7 for compilation and runtime  
• **OpenRewrite 6.13.0**: Automated code transformation engine  
  - `UpgradeToJava21` recipe for language version migration  
  - `UpgradeSpringBoot_3_0` recipe for framework modernization  
• **Amazon Q CLI**: AI-powered code analysis and manual fixes  
  - Model: Claude 4 Sonnet for intelligent problem resolution  
  - Manual remediation of deprecated APIs and compatibility issues  
  
## Code Changes 📝  
  
• **Security.java**: Migrated `javax.security.cert.*` → `java.security.cert.*` with modern CertificateFactory  
• **Encoder.java**: Replaced deprecated `Date(1999, 0, 1)` constructor with Calendar API  
• **MockTest.java**: Fixed unchecked operations with proper generics and @SuppressWarnings annotations  
• **pom.xml**: Updated Java version property and Maven compiler plugin configuration  
• **Test Classes**: Converted JUnit 4 → JUnit 5 annotations and assertion methods  
• **Controller Classes**: Applied Jakarta validation namespace migration  
  
## Time Savings Estimate ⏱️  
  
• **OpenRewrite Automation**: 47 minutes saved (20m Java upgrade + 27m Spring Boot upgrade)  
• **Manual Remediation**: ~2-3 hours of developer time for deprecated API fixes  
• **Testing & Validation**: ~1 hour for comprehensive test suite execution  
• **Total Estimated Savings**: 4-5 hours of manual development work  
• **Actual Project Duration**: ~45 minutes with AI assistance  
  
## Next Steps 🚀  
  
### Immediate Validation  
• ✅ Run full regression test suite in staging environment  
• ✅ Performance benchmarking against Java 8 baseline  
• ✅ Security vulnerability scanning with updated dependencies  
  
### Recommended Improvements  
• 🔧 Resolve duplicate JSON library warning by excluding conflicting dependencies  
• 🔧 Consider upgrading to Spring Boot 3.2+ for latest security patches  
• 🔧 Implement Java 21 virtual threads for improved concurrency  
• 🔧 Leverage pattern matching and record classes for modern Java idioms  
• 🔧 Update AWS SDK to latest version for enhanced Java 21 compatibility  
  
### Production Readiness  
• 📋 Update deployment pipelines for Java 21 runtime  
• 📋 Monitor application startup time and memory usage improvements  
• 📋 Document breaking changes for dependent services  
• 📋 Plan rollback strategy with Java 8 compatibility testing

author: ayqy
body:
The settings panel (which is part of popup.html) was missing its CSS styles because popup.css was not being processed by Vite during the build.

This was due to popup.css not being imported in its corresponding entry point, src/popup/popup.ts.

By adding `import './popup.css';` to src/popup/popup.ts, Vite now includes popup.css in the build, outputting it to dist/src/popup/popup.css where popup.html can correctly link to it.

author: arusu0629
body:
## 概要
Issue #40 の実装: アプリ全体のパフォーマンス最適化とApp Store提出前の最終品質保証を実施。主要な改善として、@Stateの統合によるViewModelパターンの導入、暗号化処理のキャッシュ化、アプリ起動時間の短縮、並列処理による検索機能の最適化を行いました。

## 変更内容

### 新規作成
- `ViewModels/ContentViewModel.swift`: ContentViewの状態管理を統合し、27個の@State変数を集約したViewModelクラス
- `Debouncer.swift`: スクロール処理とフィルタリング用のデバウンス機能を提供するユーティリティクラス

### 修正
- `ContentView.swift`: 27個の@State変数を@StateObject ContentViewModelに統合、重複する初期化ロジックを削除
- `EatLockApp.swift`: アプリ起動時の初期化処理を並列化し、非重要なタスクを遅延実行に変更
- `ActionLogRepository.swift`: 暗号化/復号化処理にLRUキャッシュを追加、バッチ処理の並列化、統計計算の最適化
- `Views/Components/LogListView.swift`: フィルタリング処理の非同期化、検索処理の並列化、結果キャッシュの実装

### 削除
- ContentViewの重複するプライベートメソッド（setupRepository、showToast、keyboardObserver系）をViewModelに移動

## 技術詳細
- **アーキテクチャの変更点**: MVVMパターンの導入によりContentViewの責務を分離、@State変数の統合でView更新頻度を削減
- **採用した技術やライブラリ**: Swift ConcurrencyのwithTaskGroupを使用した並列処理、Combineを活用したリアクティブプログラミング
- **その他、特筆すべき技術的判断**: 
  - デバウンス機能によりスクロール時のパフォーマンス向上（60fps維持）
  - LRUキャッシュ（最大100エントリ）による暗号化処理の高速化
  - 統計計算の30秒キャッシュによりCPU使用率削減

## 動作確認
- [x] 機能の基本動作確認
- [x] エラーハンドリングの確認  
- [x] 既存機能への影響確認
- [x] ビルドエラーがないことの確認
- [x] アプリ起動時間の短縮確認（目標1.5秒以内）
- [x] スクロール性能の改善確認（60fps維持）
- [x] メモリ使用量の最適化確認

## 関連Issue

# Replace mock CLI commands with real reflex-hosting-cli package imports

## Summary

This PR replaces the mock CLI command system with direct imports from the actual `reflex-hosting-cli` package, enabling automated and always up-to-date CLI documentation generation. 

**Key changes:**
- **Removed 200+ lines of mock CLI commands** that were hardcoded and could become outdated
- **Added direct imports** from `reflex_cli.v2` modules (deployments, apps, project, secrets, vmtypes_regions, cli)
- **Created Click command wrappers** for core functions (login, logout, deploy) to enable documentation introspection
- **All 33 CLI commands across 8 sections** now use real package introspection instead of mock data

The documentation generation process remains the same - the `process_command` function now processes real CLI commands instead of mock ones, ensuring the docs always reflect the actual CLI behavior.

author: roasbeef
body:
In this PR, we implement comprehensive taproot RBF cooperative channel closing support for LND. The implementation extends the existing RBF cooperative close protocol to support taproot channels using MuSig2 signatures and introduces a JIT (Just-In-Time) nonce pattern for secure and efficient nonce management during RBF iterations.

## wire + state machine changes

The implementation introduces taproot-specific wire protocol extensions for the `shutdown`, `closing_complete`, and `closing_sig` messages. The `shutdown` message now carries closee nonces for taproot channels, while `closing_complete` uses `PartialSigWithNonce` structures that bundle partial signatures with next-round nonces. The `closing_sig` message uses separate `PartialSig` and `NextCloseeNonce` fields to optimize nonce delivery timing.

The cooperative close state machine has been extended with taproot channel detection through the `IsTaproot()` method and comprehensive nonce state management. The implementation maintains separate `LocalMusigSession` and `RemoteMusigSession` contexts for handling the asymmetric closer/closee roles in the taproot closing flow.

New signature extraction and validation helpers handle both taproot partial signatures and traditional ECDSA signatures with proper type validation. The `partialSigToWireSig`, `extractTaprootSigAndNonce`, and `validateAndExtractSigAndNonce` functions provide robust signature handling while maintaining backward compatibility.

The state transitions have been updated to properly initialize MuSig2 sessions with appropriate closee nonces, handle signature preparation for both channel types, and manage the complex nonce rotation required for secure RBF iterations. The implementation includes comprehensive error handling for taproot-specific validation requirements.


Fixes https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/issues/9662

author: matfra
body:
I've integrated the Flask-based configuration server directly into the main fenetre.py application. This unification simplifies deployment and process management by running a single main Python process.

Key changes:
- I modified `fenetre.py` to launch the Flask app (from `config_server.py`) in a separate thread, managed by `fenetre.py`'s configuration and lifecycle (start, stop, reload via SIGHUP).
- I added a new `config_server` section to the main YAML configuration file (`config.yaml`) to control the embedded Flask server (enable, host, port).
- I adapted `config_server.py` to be importable:
    - Removed standalone execution.
    - Routes now fetch necessary configurations (e.g., main config file path, PID file path) from `app.config`, which is populated by `fenetre.py`.
- I updated `config.example.yaml` with the new `config_server` section.
- I added `waitress` to `requirements.txt` as the preferred WSGI server for the Flask app.
- I updated `Dockerfile` to include `config_server.py` and its `static` UI assets in the image, and to ensure `waitress` is installed.

body:
# 💾 Phase 2.2: LangGraph Checkpointing & Memory Management

## Summary

This PR implements **Phase 2.2: LangGraph Checkpointing & Memory Management**, adding optional conversation persistence and rollback capabilities using LangGraph's MemorySaver integration. This establishes the foundation for long-running workflows, multi-session DAGs, and conversation persistence while maintaining full backward compatibility.

## 🚀 Key Features

### **Memory Management & Checkpointing**
- **Optional Checkpointing**: Defaults to off for backward compatibility, can be enabled per execution
- **Thread-Scoped Memory**: Multi-session conversation isolation with unique thread IDs
- **LangGraph MemorySaver Integration**: Native checkpointing with LangGraph 0.5.1
- **Rollback Mechanisms**: Failed execution recovery with checkpoint restoration
- **TTL-Based Cleanup**: Automatic checkpoint expiration and memory optimization

### **Error Resilience & Circuit Breakers**
- **Centralized Error Policies**: Retry logic, circuit breaker patterns, and fallback strategies per agent
- **Circuit Breaker Patterns**: Configurable failure thresholds per agent with recovery timeouts
- **Retry Strategies**: Exponential backoff, linear backoff, adaptive, and fixed interval delays
- **Error Classification**: Timeout, LLM, validation, resource exhaustion, network, and configuration errors

### **Enhanced CLI Integration**
- **New CLI Flags**: `--enable-checkpoints`, `--thread-id`, `--rollback-last-checkpoint`
- **Performance Comparison**: `--compare-modes` and `--benchmark-runs` for statistical analysis
- **Enhanced DAG Visualization**: Checkpoint nodes (💾) and circuit breaker indicators (🔌)

## 📦 New Components

### **Core Infrastructure**
- **`memory_manager.py`**: LangGraph MemorySaver integration with thread ID scoping
- **`error_policies.py`**: Centralized retry logic and circuit breaker patterns
- **Enhanced `real_orchestrator.py`**: Optional checkpointing integration with memory manager
- **Updated `cli.py`**: New Phase 2.2 CLI flags and rollback mode handling

### **Enhanced Features**
- **Enhanced DAG Visualization**: Shows checkpoint-enabled nodes and error handling routes
- **Comprehensive Test Coverage**: Memory management, error policies, and integration tests
- **State Serialization**: Robust CogniVaultState persistence with comprehensive type handling

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### **Memory Manager Architecture**
```python
class CogniVaultMemoryManager:
    def __init__(self, config: CheckpointConfig):
        self.config = config
        self.memory_saver: Optional[MemorySaver] = None
        self.checkpoints: Dict[str, List[CheckpointInfo]] = {}
        
        if self.config.enabled:
            self.memory_saver = MemorySaver()
```

### **Error Policy Integration**
```python
class ErrorPolicyManager:
    def _setup_default_policies(self):
        self.policies["refiner"] = ErrorPolicy(
            policy_type=ErrorPolicyType.RETRY_WITH_BACKOFF, 
            retry_config=RetryConfig(max_attempts=2)
        )
        self.policies["historian"] = ErrorPolicy(
            policy_type=ErrorPolicyType.CIRCUIT_BREAKER, 
            circuit_breaker_config=CircuitBreakerConfig(failure_threshold=3)
        )
```

### **CLI Integration**
```bash
# Enable checkpointing with custom thread
make run QUESTION="Your question" ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1 THREAD_ID=my-session

# Rollback to last checkpoint on failure
make run QUESTION="Your question" ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1 ROLLBACK_LAST_CHECKPOINT=1

# Performance benchmarking with checkpointing
make run QUESTION="Your question" COMPARE_MODES=1 BENCHMARK_RUNS=5 ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1
```

## 📋 Files Changed

### **New Files**
- `src/cognivault/langraph/memory_manager.py` - LangGraph MemorySaver integration
- `src/cognivault/langraph/error_policies.py` - Centralized error policies
- `tests/langraph/test_memory_manager.py` - Memory management test suite
- `tests/langraph/test_error_policies.py` - Error policy test coverage
- `tests/langraph/test_checkpointing_integration.py` - Integration tests

### **Enhanced Files**
- `src/cognivault/langraph/real_orchestrator.py` - Memory manager integration
- `src/cognivault/cli.py` - New CLI flags for checkpointing
- `src/cognivault/diagnostics/visualize_dag.py` - Enhanced DAG visualization
- `Makefile` - Updated with Phase 2.2 CLI flags
- `README.md` - Comprehensive Phase 2.2 documentation
- `src/cognivault/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` - Updated architectural documentation

## ✅ Testing & Quality Assurance

### **Comprehensive Test Coverage**
- **Memory Manager Tests**: Checkpoint creation, rollback, serialization, error scenarios
- **Error Policy Tests**: Retry policies, circuit breaker patterns, decorator functionality  
- **Integration Tests**: End-to-end memory management with error policies
- **CLI Tests**: New checkpoint flags and rollback mode handling
- **DAG Visualization Tests**: Enhanced node labels and checkpoint indicators

### **Quality Checks**
- ✅ **All mypy type errors resolved** (164 source files checked)
- ✅ **Code formatting applied** (black + ruff)
- ✅ **Performance tested** (No regression when checkpointing disabled)
- ✅ **Backward compatibility maintained** (All existing functionality preserved)

## 🧪 Example Usage Workflows

### **Research Session with Checkpointing**
```bash
# Start a research session with checkpointing
make run QUESTION="What are the implications of AI governance?" \
    ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1 THREAD_ID=ai-governance-research

# Continue the conversation in the same session
make run QUESTION="How do different countries approach AI regulation?" \
    ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1 THREAD_ID=ai-governance-research  

# If execution fails, rollback to last checkpoint
make run QUESTION="What are the enforcement mechanisms?" \
    ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1 THREAD_ID=ai-governance-research ROLLBACK_LAST_CHECKPOINT=1
```

### **Performance Comparison Testing**
```bash
# Benchmark with and without checkpointing
make run QUESTION="Complex analysis question" COMPARE_MODES=1 BENCHMARK_RUNS=5
make run QUESTION="Complex analysis question" COMPARE_MODES=1 BENCHMARK_RUNS=5 ENABLE_CHECKPOINTS=1
```

## 📊 Performance & Memory Impact

### **Checkpointing Performance**
- **Overhead**: Minimal when disabled (default behavior)
- **Memory Usage**: Efficient thread-scoped storage with TTL cleanup
- **Serialization**: Optimized CogniVaultState persistence
- **Cleanup**: Automatic checkpoint expiration and thread management

### **Error Policy Benefits**
- **Resilience**: Circuit breaker patterns prevent cascade failures
- **Efficiency**: Intelligent retry strategies with exponential backoff
- **Observability**: Comprehensive error tracking and recovery metrics

## 🔄 Backward Compatibility

### **Seamless Migration**
- **Default Behavior**: Checkpointing disabled by default - no impact on existing workflows
- **CLI Compatibility**: All existing CLI commands work unchanged
- **Performance**: No regression when checkpointing disabled
- **Configuration**: Optional features only activate when explicitly enabled

### **Upgrade Path**
- **Incremental Adoption**: Users can enable checkpointing per execution
- **Thread Management**: Auto-generated thread IDs when not specified
- **Rollback Safety**: Rollback only works when checkpointing is enabled

- **Adaptive Policies**: Success rate-based retry adjustments

author: copilot
body:
The release workflow was failing due to insufficient permissions for the GitHub Actions bot to create git tags and GitHub releases. The workflow uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` but lacked explicit permission declarations.

## Problem
The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) was attempting to:
1. Create and push git tags: `git push origin "v${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"`
2. Create GitHub releases using `softprops/action-gh-release@v1`

Both operations were failing with permission errors because the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions were insufficient.

## Solution
Added explicit `permissions` section to the release workflow:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: write
  metadata: read
```

- `contents: write` - Required for creating git tags and GitHub releases
- `metadata: read` - Required for reading repository metadata

## Changes
- Added 3 lines to `.github/workflows/release.yml` (lines 7-9)
- No changes to existing workflow logic or functionality
- YAML syntax validated and confirmed working

This minimal change ensures the GitHub Actions bot has the necessary permissions to successfully execute the release workflow without breaking any existing functionality.

Fixes #5.

author: joshrowley
body:
### Summary

This PR introduces a new GitHub Action workflow that automatically checks whether the Rails version specified in our `Gemfile.lock` matches the latest stable release available on RubyGems.

- Resolves https://github.com/joshrowley/summit/issues/19

### Details

- **Workflow location:** `.github/workflows/check-latest-rails.yml`
- **Triggers:** Runs on every push, pull request, and manual dispatch.
- **Steps:**
  1. Checks out the repository.
  2. Extracts the current Rails version from `Gemfile.lock`.
  3. Fetches the latest stable Rails version from RubyGems.
  4. Compares the two versions.
  5. Fails the workflow with a clear error message if the project is not using the latest Rails version.

### Motivation

Keeping Rails up to date ensures we benefit from the latest features, bug fixes, and security patches. This automated check will help us stay current and reduce technical debt.

### Outcome

- Developers will be notified via CI if the Rails version is outdated.
- Encourages regular updates and improved security posture.

author: copilot
body:
This PR significantly expands HealIQ's restoration druid spell suggestions by adding 8 new rules for commonly overlooked abilities, addressing the core issue of missing coverage for important spells.

## New Rules Added

The following high-priority restoration druid abilities are now tracked and suggested:

1. **Tranquility** - Emergency healing cooldown for 4+ damaged allies
2. **Incarnation: Tree of Life** - Transformation cooldown for high damage phases  
3. **Ironbark** - Damage reduction cooldown with intelligent target checking
4. **Efflorescence** - Ground-targeted persistent AoE healing
5. **Flourish** - HoT duration extension when multiple effects are expiring
6. **Nature's Swiftness** - Instant cast proc availability
7. **Barkskin** - Self-defense damage reduction
8. **Trinket Usage** - Active healing trinket detection for both slots

## Technical Implementation

### Enhanced Tracking System
- Added comprehensive spell ID definitions for all new abilities
- Implemented trinket cooldown monitoring for slots 13 & 14
- Enhanced combat log parsing to track Efflorescence placement and duration
- Expanded player buff monitoring for defensive/healing procs

### Intelligent Rule Logic
- **Tranquility**: Triggered when 4+ allies recently took damage (emergency situations)
- **Incarnation**: Suggested during high damage phases (3+ recent damage)
- **Ironbark**: Only suggested when target needs damage reduction and doesn't have it
- **Efflorescence**: Suggested when not active and 2+ allies took damage
- **Flourish**: Suggested when 2+ HoTs are expiring within 6 seconds
- **Trinket**: Detects active healing trinkets and suggests usage

### Priority System
Restructured the entire priority system with proper ordering:
1. Emergency cooldowns (Tranquility, Incarnation)
2. Damage reduction (Ironbark) 
3. AoE healing (Wild Growth, Efflorescence)
4. HoT management (Flourish, Lifebloom refresh)
5. Proc utilization (Nature's Swiftness, Clearcasting)
6. Basic coverage (Swiftmend, Rejuvenation)
7. Utility (Trinkets, Barkskin)

## User Experience

### Configuration
- All new rules are configurable via `/healiq rules` commands
- Updated options UI to accommodate new rules (expanded height)
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing configurations

### Commands Enhanced
```
/healiq rules list  # Now shows all 13 rules
/healiq rules enable ironbark  # Enable specific new rules
/healiq test engine  # Test all new rule evaluations
```

## Quality Assurance

- ✅ All files pass Lua syntax validation
- ✅ Zero warnings/errors from luacheck linting
- ✅ Addon structure validation passes
- ✅ Version consistency verified across all files
- ✅ Comprehensive test coverage for rule logic

## Backward Compatibility

All existing functionality is preserved:
- Existing rule configurations maintained
- No breaking changes to saved variables
- Original 5 rules continue to work as before

This enhancement transforms HealIQ from covering basic restoration druid spells to providing comprehensive coverage of the full toolkit, including the defensive cooldowns, ground effects, and major healing CDs that are often overlooked in healing rotations.

Fixes #7.

author: dao-jun
body:
### Motivation

In our pulsar cluster, we have encountered an extremely strange problem.
A topic has been running for a long time, but at a time, it starts `fenced` for a long time(more than 3 hours, until we unload it manually).

After we analysis the heap dump and broker log, we find the root cause:

For some reason the CAS operation in `OpAddEntry.initiate()` failed, but it logs `initiate with unexpected state OPEN, expect OPEN state.`
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e287e31-3a1c-48f6-8d90-5f2b8f16bd0b)
Which means the `state` is `OPEN`, but the CAS operation still fails.
Because of the CAS operation failed, the request did not send to bookies.

The next request passed the CAS operation and sent to bookies and received the response, when doing callback, it will check the `ml.pendingAddEntries`.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20ca5a69-8874-4662-9ff6-0f281502d7ff)
It polls the 1st entry, but the 1st entry did not send to bookies, so it will `firstInQueue.failed(...)` the 1st entry, and the topic will be fenced.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82ace071-6296-459a-99d9-62f8161efd4e)


But the 2nd entry will always hang there, **because it only fails the 1st entry but do nothing to itself**. So the topic keeps fencing and never be unfenced.


The PR change maybe could causes message out of ordering, so do not merge.

author: titobouzout
body:
It adds the optimization you suggested on discord, recorded here https://github.com/ryansolid/dom-expressions/issues/390

It considers spreads and computed keys, such `{[store.key]: "ja"}`, on which case it will keep using a getter.  It also considers `@once`.

It may be possible that we want this optimization in other places 🤔 , as when I search for `"get"` similar code popups around. Can you please have a look? Thanks!

I'm like 95% confident this won't break stuff, but honestly I'm not sure.  

Initially the recursion was a bit messy, I have just simplified it.

## Problem
The top navigation menu appeared too narrow on wide screens (PC/Mac), making the layout look awkward with large margins on both sides. This was caused by a restrictive `max-w-screen-lg` class applied to the navigation container inside `_includes/layout/header.html`.

## Solution
Updated the navigation container's max-width constraint from `max-w-screen-lg` to `max-w-screen-xl` to allow the menu to span a more natural width on large screens while maintaining proper alignment and responsiveness.

## Changes Made
- **File:** `_includes/layout/header.html`
- **Change:** Line 7 - Updated `max-w-screen-lg` to `max-w-screen-xl` in the navigation flex container
- **Impact:** Single line change, minimal and surgical fix

## Before & After Screenshots

### Before (Narrow Navigation)
![Before - Narrow Navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9dcfa788-1805-4cd4-a439-f18f7b23ad9e)

### After (Improved Width)
![After - Improved Navigation Width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1036f679-0077-43c3-ac90-e42ce71d2a16)

## Testing Verified
- ✅ Desktop navigation now spans appropriate width on large screens
- ✅ Logo remains left-aligned, menu items remain right-aligned
- ✅ Horizontal padding maintained (px-6 lg:px-24 in header container)
- ✅ Mobile responsiveness preserved (hamburger menu shows correctly on small screens)
- ✅ No overstretching on ultra-wide screens (max-w-screen-xl = ~1280px constraint)
- ✅ Site builds successfully with Jekyll + Tailwind CSS

## Technical Details
The change aligns the navigation container width with the header container, both now using `max-w-screen-xl`. This creates a consistent layout where:
- `max-w-screen-lg` = ~1024px (too narrow for modern screens)
- `max-w-screen-xl` = ~1280px (appropriate for wide screens without overstretching)

The existing horizontal padding (`px-6 lg:px-24`) ensures content doesn't touch screen edges on any screen size.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> The top navigation menu appears too narrow on wide screens (PC/Mac), making the layout look awkward, as shown in the provided screenshot ![image1](image1). This is due to restrictive max-width classes (`max-w-screen-lg`) applied to the header/nav container in `_includes/layout/header.html`, causing the menu to float in the center with large margins on the sides. 
> 
> **Task:**
> - Update `_includes/layout/header.html` to make the desktop navigation menu span a more natural width on large screens.
> - Replace `max-w-screen-lg` with `max-w-screen-xl` (or remove the max-width constraint if appropriate) in the main flex container inside the header.
> - Ensure horizontal padding is still present so content doesn't touch the edges (use `px-6 lg:px-24` or similar).
> - The logo should remain left-aligned, and the menu right-aligned, using flex.
> - Confirm that the menu remains visually appealing and not overly stretched on large monitors, and that mobile responsiveness is not affected.
> 
> No other cosmetic changes; only address the desktop/top-menu width issue.
>

This pull request introduces a robust and comprehensive unit test suite for the `ResourceDistribution` generator. The primary goal is to validate the generator's behavior across its full feature set, ensuring its output is correct and its error handling is reliable.

## Key Contributions 

- **Expanded Test Coverage**: Adds tests for core features that were previously untested, including:
  - Data generation from `literalSources`.
  - Applying `resourceOptions` (labels, annotations) to the inner resource.
  - Advanced namespace targeting with `matchExpressions` and `excludedNamespaces`.

- **Robust Assertions**: The test validation logic has been refactored to unmarshal the expected and actual YAML into `unstructured.Unstructured` objects. These objects are then compared directly, making the tests more reliable and independent of formatting or key order.

## Feat: 更新至 Emby 4.8.11 并简化激活流程

### ✨ 特性 (Features)

* **版本升级**：Emby Server 已更新至最新的 **4.8.11** 版本。
* **简化激活方式**：通过直接修改核心 `dll` 与 `js` 文件实现激活，不再需要依赖 Nginx 进行中间人攻击 (MITM)。这使得整个方案更加简洁、高效。
* **内置重定向**：将 `mb3admin.com` 的验证请求重定向至一个公共的 Cloudflare Worker 服务，用户无需再自行搭建反向代理服务器。

### 📝 改进背景 (Reason for Improvement)

此更新解决了旧方案中存在的主要问题。原有的 Nginx + Emby 容器通过 Docker Network 互联的方案，存在两个痛点：

1.  **HTTPS 密钥维护复杂**：需要定期手动更新 Nginx 容器内的 HTTPS 密钥，操作繁琐且容易出错。
2.  **网络模式限制**：使用 `docker network` 会导致 Emby 容器无法使用 `network_mode: host`。这对于希望简化网络配置、直接暴露端口或进行硬件转码的用户来说非常不便。

author: gilfeather
body:
This pull request introduces significant security and monitoring enhancements for a static site infrastructure using AWS. Key changes include the addition of security headers via a CloudFront function, enhanced S3 bucket policies, and new monitoring capabilities with CloudWatch. The changes improve compliance, security, and observability while maintaining flexibility through configurable Terraform variables.

### Security Enhancements:
* Added a CloudFront function (`security-headers.js`) to inject security headers like `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Content-Security-Policy`, and others into HTTP responses.
* Enhanced S3 bucket policies to enforce secure transport (HTTPS-only) and deny connections using outdated TLS versions.
* Updated the CloudFront distribution to associate the security headers function during the `viewer-response` event.

### Monitoring Improvements:
* Introduced CloudWatch log groups and metric alarms to monitor CloudFront error rates and S3 events, ensuring better observability.
* Added an optional S3 bucket notification system integrated with EventBridge for capturing object creation and deletion events.

### Configuration Flexibility:
* Added new Terraform variables (`enable_security_headers`, `enable_enhanced_s3_policy`, etc.) to toggle security and monitoring features. Defaults are set to enable these features by default. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-05b5a57c136b6ff596500bcbfdcff145ef6cddea2a0e86d184d9daa9a65a288eR188-R218) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-74a0fde6487cd81c1e9caa5d1f82161ac3e344fa9ecd4dc85049c6fce8796737R45-R51)

### Miscellaneous:
* Updated the S3 bucket naming convention to include the AWS account ID and region for better uniqueness and traceability.
* Adjusted the basic S3 bucket policy resource to conditionally apply based on whether the enhanced policy is enabled.

body:
# Description of Changes

- **What was changed:**  
  - Renamed top-level directories: `stirling-pdf` → `app/core`, `common` → `app/common`, `proprietary` → `app/proprietary`.  
  - Updated all path references in `.gitattributes`, GitHub workflows (`.github/workflows/*`), scripts (`.github/scripts/*`), `.gitignore`, Dockerfiles, license files, and template settings to reflect the new structure.  
  - Added a new CI job `check-generateOpenApiDocs` to generate and upload OpenAPI documentation.  
  - Removed redundant `@Autowired` annotations from `TempFileShutdownHook` and `UnlockPDFFormsController`.  
  - Minor formatting and comment adjustments in YAML templates and resource files.

- **Why the change was made:**  
  - To introduce a clear `app/` directory hierarchy for core, common, and proprietary modules, improving organization and maintainability.  
  - To ensure continuous integration and Docker builds continue to work seamlessly with the reorganized structure.  
  - To automate OpenAPI documentation generation as part of the CI pipeline.

author: victoryforce
body:
What was done in the code (mainly in the headers) of imageio:

- Removed conditional provision of dummy implementations in header files if darktable is not built with the corresponding functionality. These dummy loader functions are simply no longer used, as we do the same in imageio.c after rewriting to a signature-based architecture.

- Instead of using `#ifdef HAVE_somefeature` in header files, we now guarantee that the header will not be included if the corresponding functionality is not built.

- Wrapped the call to `dt_libraw_lookup_makermodel` in an #ifdef instead of always calling the function with that name, but providing a dummy implementation if darktable is built without libraw.

- Removed duplicate include of `imageio_libraw.h`.

- Replaced include guards with `#pragma once`.

author: copilot
body:
The `word_timestamps` dictionary was using words as keys, causing duplicate words in a sentence to overwrite each other. Consider this scenario:

```python
# Sentence: "someday something in something"
# Old implementation result:
{'someday': 1.0, 'something': 3.0, 'in': 2.5}
# Problem: First occurrence of "something" at timestamp 2.0 was lost!

# New implementation result:
{1.0: 'someday', 2.0: 'something', 2.5: 'in', 3.0: 'something'}
# Solution: Both occurrences preserved with timestamps as keys
```

## Changes Made

### 1. Modified `_extract_word_timestamps()`
- **Before**: Returns `{word: end_time}` causing overwrites when words repeat
- **After**: Returns `{end_time: word}` using unique timestamps as keys
- Removed unnecessary punctuation handling that created duplicate entries
- Now preserves ALL word occurrences regardless of repetition

### 2. Updated `_find_last_word_end_time()`
- Completely rewritten to work with the new `{timestamp: word}` structure
- When multiple occurrences of a word exist, correctly returns the latest timestamp
- Maintains robust fallback logic for partial word matching
- Improved debugging output to show available words

## Impact
This is a minimal, surgical change affecting only the two functions mentioned in the issue. The fix ensures that:
- ✅ All word occurrences are preserved in timestamp data
- ✅ Last word lookup correctly identifies the most recent occurrence
- ✅ No other parts of the codebase are affected
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility for the calling code

The solution directly addresses the core problem where repeated words like "something" in "someday something in something" would lose their earlier timestamps, which was critical for accurate speech-to-text processing timing.

Fixes #9.

author: shyok21
body:
### Problem
Currently, moment fails to parse 5-digit inputs like `21530` when using the format `eHHmm`. It expects a space between the weekday and the time part (i.e., `2 1530`), which causes the parse to silently fail or produce `Invalid date`.

### What has been fixed
To handle such compact formats, a conditional check is added inside the `configFromStringAndFormat` function. If the format is exactly `'eHHmm'` and the input is 5 characters long, we convert:
- `eHHmm` → `e HHmm`
- `'21530'` → `'2 1530'`

This allows the parser to treat weekday (`e`) and time (`HHmm`) correctly, without requiring changes to the parsing logic or regex tokens.

### Why this approach?
Other options were considered:
- Modifying the parsing token regex for `'e'` or `'HHmm'`, but that would have introduced complexity and risked regressions in other areas.
- Writing a custom parse token handler for `'eHHmm'`, but it felt overkill for such a narrow use case.

Instead, this inline fix keeps the logic isolated to a single known edge case and doesn't interfere with existing formats or locale behavior.

### Additional Notes
- Test cases have been added to ensure both 5-digit (`21530`) and 6-digit (`021530`) inputs are handled correctly.
- No changes were made to existing parsing behavior for other formats.

Please let me know if you'd prefer this logic moved to a more central parsing utility, happy to revise based on feedback.

Closes #6116

body:
Enhanced the `.github/pyproject_versions.py` script to address version coherence issues and prevent manual version bumps that forget to use bumpver.

## Problem
The original issue identified a need to check version coherence between files managed by bumpver to avoid manual bumps that forget to use the proper versioning tool. The three files that should always have synchronized versions are:
- `codecarbon/_version.py`
- `docs/edit/conf.py`
- `pyproject.toml`

## Solution
Added comprehensive version coherence checking functionality:

### New Features
- **Version coherence validation**: Automatically checks that all three bumpver-managed files have consistent versions
- **New CLI option**: `--check_coherence` for standalone coherence validation
- **Automatic prevention**: All operations now validate version coherence before proceeding
- **Clear error reporting**: Detailed messages identify which files have inconsistent versions

### Key Functions Added
```python
def get_version_from_file(filepath: str, pattern: str) -> str:
    """Extract version from a file using regex patterns"""

def get_all_versions() -> dict:
    """Read versions from all three bumpver-managed files"""

def check_version_coherence() -> bool:
    """Validate version consistency across files"""
```

### Usage Examples
```bash
# Check version coherence only
python .github/pyproject_versions.py --check_coherence

# Normal operations now include automatic coherence checking
python .github/pyproject_versions.py --replace True
```

### Error Prevention
When versions are inconsistent, the script now:
- Displays clear error messages showing which files have different versions
- Prevents operations that could lead to further inconsistencies
- Guides users to use 'bumpver' for consistent version updates

Example output for inconsistent versions:
```
✗ Version coherence check failed! Versions are inconsistent:
  pyproject.toml [tool.bumpver] current_version: 3.0.3
  codecarbon/_version.py __version__: 3.0.4
  docs/edit/conf.py release: 3.0.3

Please use 'bumpver' to update versions consistently across all files.
```

### Backward Compatibility
- All existing functionality preserved
- CI workflows continue to work unchanged
- Fixed existing bug in `--only_package_version` output (was referencing wrong variable)

The improvements ensure that version coherence is maintained across all bumpver-managed files and help prevent the manual version update issues described in the original issue.

Fixes #904.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR addresses inconsistencies in the `imglib` library and propagates changes consistently throughout the codebase. The changes improve the build system structure while maintaining compatibility with existing test files.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Function Naming Inconsistencies
The library had mismatched function declarations and implementations:
- **Header** (`imglib.h`): declared `img_pixel_put`
- **Implementation** (`imglib.c`): implemented `img_put_pixel`
- **Test files**: called `img_put_pixel`

**Fix**: Updated header to match implementation and usage patterns.

### 2. Structure Compatibility Issues
Test files expected `t_data.img` to be a direct image pointer (`void*`) for use with `mlx_put_image_to_window()`, but the library defined it as a nested `t_img` struct.

**Before**:
```c
// Library definition
typedef struct s_data {
    void    *mlx_ptr;
    void    *win_ptr;
    t_img   img;        // Nested struct
} t_data;

// Test usage (broken)
mlx_put_image_to_window(mlx, window, shape.img, 0, 0);  // Type error
```

**After**:
```c
// Updated library definition
typedef struct s_data {
    void    *mlx_ptr;
    void    *win_ptr;
    void    *img;           // Direct image pointer
    char    *addr;
    int     bits_per_pixel;
    int     line_length;
    int     endian;
} t_data;

// Test usage (works)
mlx_put_image_to_window(mlx, window, shape.img, 0, 0);  // ✓
```

### 3. Missing Functions
Added `img_init_data()` function that test files were calling but wasn't implemented in the library.

### 4. Build System Issues
- **variables.mk**: Fixed `COLORS_DIR` path (was incorrectly pointing to `imglib` instead of `colors`)
- **Makefiles**: Added missing colors library dependencies and include paths
- **Consistency**: Standardized all Makefiles to use common variables and patterns

## Changes Made

### Library Updates (`my_libraries/imglib/`)
- **imglib.h**: Fixed function declaration, restructured `t_data`, added `img_init_data` declaration
- **imglib.c**: Updated implementations to work with new structure, fixed MLX function name
- **Makefile**: Already following good patterns, no changes needed

### Build System Improvements
- **variables.mk**: Fixed `COLORS_DIR = $(MY_LIBS_DIR)/colors`
- **All Makefiles**: 
  - Now use `variables.mk` for consistent `CC` and `CFLAGS`
  - Added `.PHONY` declarations
  - Standardized clean targets with `$(RM)`
  - Added colors library dependencies where needed

### Project Structure
```
my_libraries/
├── imglib/     # Core image manipulation library
├── colors/     # Color definitions and utilities

author: abujabarmubarak
body: ### Problem Fixes issue #61841 — calling `.rolling().mean()` twice on a copied DataFrame was returning all NaNs on the second run. This happened due to a slicing operation (`[::self.step]`) in `_apply_columnwise`, which broke result alignment when overwriting the same column. ### Solution Removed the `[:: self.step]` slicing from the return statement. This restores full alignment and fixes the regression. ### Test Case Tested locally with this code: ```python df = pd.DataFrame({"Close": list(range(1, 31))}) df = df.copy() df["SMA20"] = df["Close"].rolling(20).mean() df["SMA20"] = df["Close"].rolling(20).mean() print(df.tail())
